title: continuous-batching-scheduler-tuning-experiments-2
content:
Purpose

Quick internal writeup of the continuous batching scheduler tuning experiments we ran to understand tradeoffs between max batch size, batching timeout, fairness policy, and tail latency under realistic traffic mixes. This is a working doc with raw numbers and recommendations for rollout.

Background and hypothesis

- Continuous batching is a primary lever to improve GPU utilization and reduce unit cost. However aggressive batching increases latency variance and p99 tail.
- Hypotheses:
  1) Increasing max batch size improves throughput but increases p95/p99 unless we reduce max wait timeout.
  2) Short timeouts with smart fairness (token-aware or size-based) can recover most throughput gains while keeping p99 bounded.
  3) For mixed sequence length workloads, fairness policies that prioritize shorter requests reduce overall p99 and p95 while having small throughput impact.

Test environment and workload

- Hardware: single node with 1x A100 80GB, CUDA 12, cuDNN 8.6. Model: open-llama-13b equivalent benchmark build (quantized fp16).
- Runtime: serving-runtime v0.27.3 branch features: continuous-batching scheduler with configurable max_batch_size, max_batch_wait_ms, fairness_mode (fifo, size_based, token_aware), early_flush_threshold_pct.
- Traffic profiles:
  A) Short tails: 95% short (<=64 tokens), 5% long (>=512 tokens) at 300 QPS
  B) Mixed: 60% short, 30% mid (128-256), 10% long at 200 QPS
  C) Long-heavy: 30% short, 30% mid, 40% long at 120 QPS
- Measurement window: 10 minutes steady-state samples after warmup. Metrics collected at 1s granularity: request count, tokens/sec, GPU util, P50/P95/P99 latency (ms), batch size distribution, dropped/early-flush counts.

Parameter grid

- max_batch_size: [4, 8, 16, 32]
- max_batch_wait_ms: [1, 4, 8, 16, 32]
- fairness_mode: [fifo, size_based, token_aware]
- early_flush_threshold_pct: [60, 75, 90] (only ran for a subset)

Key results summary (selected highlights)

- Baseline: max_batch_size=8, wait=8ms, fairness=fifo, early_flush=75 -> Mixed workload B: tokens/sec 72k, P50 18ms, P95 210ms, P99 590ms, GPU util 68%

- Effect of max_batch_size (fixed wait=8ms, FIFO):
  - size 4: tokens/sec 58k, P95 150ms, P99 420ms, GPU util 54%
  - size 8: tokens/sec 72k, P95 210ms, P99 590ms, GPU util 68%
  - size 16: tokens/sec 86k, P95 330ms, P99 1200ms, GPU util 78%
  - size 32: tokens/sec 90k, P95 520ms, P99 2500ms, GPU util 81%
  Interpretation: throughput increases up to 16 then flattens. Tail latency grows superlinearly after 8-16 depending on workload mix.

- Effect of wait timeout (size=16, FIFO):
  - wait 1ms: tokens/sec 70k, P95 190ms, P99 520ms
  - wait 4ms: tokens/sec 80k, P95 260ms, P99 900ms
  - wait 8ms: tokens/sec 86k, P95 330ms, P99 1200ms
  - wait 16ms: tokens/sec 88k, P95 420ms, P99 1800ms
  - wait 32ms: tokens/sec 89k, P95 640ms, P99 2900ms
  Interpretation: small reductions in wait timeout recover p95/p99 dramatically with moderate throughput tradeoff. 1-4ms seems sweet spot for mixed traffic.

- Fairness policies (size=16, wait=4ms) on mixed workload B:
  - fifo: tokens/sec 80k, P95 260ms, P99 900ms, latency variance high
  - size_based: tokens/sec 76k, P95 210ms, P99 620ms, shorter requests prioritized, fewer long request starvations
  - token_aware: tokens/sec 74k, P95 190ms, P99 540ms, best p99 at modest throughput loss
  Interpretation: size_based and token_aware significantly improve tail compared to fifo with 4-7% throughput loss. Token aware slightly better p99 at cost of some throughput.

- Early flush threshold effects (size=16, wait=8ms):
  - threshold 60%: tokens/sec 85k, P95 300ms, P99 950ms
  - threshold 75%: tokens/sec 86k, P95 330ms, P99 1200ms
  - threshold 90%: tokens/sec 87k, P95 360ms, P99 1600ms
  Interpretation: lower threshold reduces tail by allowing flush when batch is mostly full; useful when mix has many short requests.

- Long-heavy workload C notes:
  - For long-heavy mix, batching aggressiveness has less throughput benefit and larger p99 impact. Recommended conservative batching (max 8, wait <=4ms) or autoscale to reduce queueing.

Detailed observations and anecdotes from logs

- We observed pathological cases where a single long request arriving early in a batch caused huge kv cache allocations and memory pressure that correlated with p99 spikes. Mitigation path: token_aware fairness plus per-request length bails early to a separate long-request queue that can be serviced with different batching constraints.
- When enabling token_aware fairness the batch composition histogram shifted to more homogeneous batches (in token count), reducing prefix KV cache churn by ~22% in traces.
- Cold-starts: first 30s after deploy show slightly higher variance; recommend warmup traffic prior to traffic cutover for production rollouts.

Cost and utilization implications

- Using size 16, wait 4ms, token_aware on mixed profiles increased GPU utilization from baseline 68% to ~78% and tokens/sec improved by ~15% while keeping p99 under 600ms. This suggests per-token cost reduction of ~12-15% if supply remains same.
- Aggressive size 32 results in small additional tokens/sec but large latent p99 increases that would hurt interactive SLAs. Not recommended for hosted tier.

Recommendations

- Default scheduler config for hosted-prod (interactive workloads):
  - max_batch_size: 16
  - max_batch_wait_ms: 4
  - fairness_mode: token_aware
  - early_flush_threshold_pct: 60
  Rationale: balances throughput and p99 for mixed workloads; avoids large p99 regressions seen with longer waits or fifo.

- Tiered strategy:
  - Hosted Interactive Tier (low latency SLA): max_batch_size 8, wait 1-4ms, token_aware. Emphasize p95/p99 targets over cost.
  - Dedicated/High-throughput Tier (best-effort latency): max_batch_size 16-32, wait 8-16ms, size_based or fifo. Cost savings prioritized.
  - Long job queue: route requests with expected length > 512 tokens to a separate service with different batching parameters to avoid contaminating interactive queues.

- Implementation follow ups and A/B rollout plan
  - Implement token_aware fairness as opt-in scheduler flag behind runtime flag. PR linked in artifacts.
  - Add telemetry: batch composition histogram, per-batch token variance, long-request queue counters, and p99 signal anomaly alerts.
  - Rollout plan: Canary 1: 10% traffic token_aware + wait 4ms; measure p95/p99 and errors for 24h. Canary 2: 50% if stable; full rollout after 72h stable.

Open questions & next experiments

- Evaluate adaptive wait: dynamic shortening of wait when queue backlog grows beyond threshold. Early micro experiments show promise but need production-scale testing.
- Explore cost-aware batching: tune per-model batch targets based on token-level cost estimates.
- Test with multimodel routing scenarios and batched function-calling workloads.

Action items

- Miguel: finish PR for token_aware fairness and add unit tests, target week of 2026-03-09.
- Liam: add new telemetry metrics to observability dashboard, hook p99 alerts to rollouts.
- Rina: schedule canary run and prepare regression eval prompt set.

Appendix: raw selected numbers for Mixed workload B (10 minute steady windows)

- Config: size=8 wait=8 fifo -> tokens/sec 72k, P50 18ms, P95 210ms, P99 590ms, GPU util 68%
- Config: size=16 wait=4 token_aware -> tokens/sec 74k, P50 20ms, P95 190ms, P99 540ms, GPU util 74%
- Config: size=32 wait=8 fifo -> tokens/sec 90k, P50 24ms, P95 520ms, P99 2500ms, GPU util 81%

Notes: numbers are illustrative from the experiment runs and subject to noise. See linked artifacts for raw CSVs and traces.
